name.text: Evaluate the Integrals involving trigonometric functions

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

To answer this question we will first consider the indefinite integral\(\displaystyle \int{@func_w@}dw\) and calculate it using two substitutions.

First, let \(u={@coef_w@}\cdot{w}\). Then, \(\frac{du}{dw}={@coef_w@}\) and so \(dw={@du/coef_w@}\).

Therefore,

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int {@func_w@}dw &= \displaystyle\int {@coef_func@}\cdot\cos^3(u)\cdot\sin^5(u)\,{@du/coef_w@}\\ &={@1/coef_w@}\displaystyle\int {@coef_func@}\cdot\cos^3(u)\cdot\sin^5(u)\,du \\ &={@1/coef_w@}\displaystyle\int {@coef_func@}\cdot\cos(u)\cdot\cos^2(u)\cdot\sin^5(u)\,du \\ & ={@1/coef_w@} \displaystyle \int {@coef_func@} \cdot \cos(u) \cdot (1-\sin^2(u)) \cdot \sin^5(u)\,du, &&\text{since, } {@recal@} \end{align} \)

Now, let \(v=\sin(u).\) Then, \(\frac{dv}{du}=\cos(u) \) and so \(du=\frac{1}{\cos(u)}dv\).

Therefore,

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int {@func_w@}dw & ={@1/coef_w@} \displaystyle \int {@coef_func@} \cdot \cos(u) \cdot  (1-\sin^2(u)) \cdot \sin^5(u)\,du \\ & ={@1/coef_w@} \displaystyle \int {@coef_func@} \cdot \cos(u) \cdot  (1-v^2) v^5\,\frac{1}{\cos(u)}dv \\ & = {@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@}\displaystyle \int(1-v^2)v^5\,dv \\ & ={@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@}\displaystyle \int v^5-v^7 \,dv \\ & ={@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@}(\frac{v^6}{6}-\frac{v^8}{8}) \\ & ={@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot (\frac{v^6}{6})-{@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot (\frac{v^8}{8}) \end{align} \)

Note that we did not include a constant of integration as this is part of a definite integral, where the constant is not needed.

Substituting back \(v=\sin(u)\) we get

\[\displaystyle \int {@func_w@}dw={@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot \left( \frac{\sin^6(u)}{6} \right)-{@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot \left(\frac{\sin^8(u)}{8} \right)\]

Similarly, substituting back \(u={@coef_w@}\cdot w\) we get

\[\displaystyle \int {@func_w@}dw={@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot \left( \frac{\sin^6({@coef_w@}\cdot w)}{6} \right)-{@(1/coef_w*coef_func)@} \cdot \left( \frac{\sin^8({@coef_w@}\cdot w)}{8} \right)\]

Therefore,

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}{@func_w@}dw & = \left[ -{@(1/coef_w*coef_func)/8@}\cdot \sin^8({@coef_w@}\cdot w)+{@(1/coef_w*coef_func)/6@}\cdot\sin^6({@coef_w@}\cdot w)\right]_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@} \\ & ={@ta@} \end{align} \)

Therefore,

\[\displaystyle \int_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}{@func_w@}dw= {@ta@}\]
